title: Sámi languages - Wikipedia
text: The Sámi languages form a branch of the Uralic language family. According to the traditional view, Sámi is within the Uralic family most closely related to the Finnic languages (Sammallahti 1998).

title: Saami, Ume
text: Language family: Uralic, Saami, Western Saami, Southwestern Saami. Number of speakers: 20.It is a dying language with only about 20 native speakers left and is spoken mainly along the Ume River in the north of Arjeplog and Arvidsjaur.

title: An introduction to Ume Sámi | The Language Closet
text: Ume Sámi is more precisely classified as a Western Sámi language, and is most closely related to Southern Sámi or åarjelsaemien gïele, while its next closest cousins are Lule Sámi and Pite Sámi, and more distantly, Northern Sámi.
